question.problem: What is the dimension of ${\text{M}}_{5\times 1}(R),$ the vector space of all $5\times 1$ matrices over $R?$
question.worked_solution:
The standard basis of ${\text{M}}_{n\times m}(R)$ contains a total of $n\cdot m$ matrices, each with one nonzero entry that is equal to $1.$ 

Thus, the standard basis of ${\text{M}}_{5\times 1}(R)$ contains $5\cdot 1=5$ elements, and is given by

$$
\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Therefore, for ${\text{M}}_{5\times 1}(R),$ we have, indeed, 

$$
\text{dim}({\text{M}}_{5\times 1}(R))=5\cdot 1=5.
$$

In general, 

$$
\text{dim}({\text{M}}_{n\times m}(R))=n\cdot m.
$$
